title: A dialog's submit button sits in DialogFooter, inside the form it submits
decision: A dialog's submit button always sits in DialogFooter, the form element wraps DialogHeader, DialogBody and DialogFooter together, the button is type="submit", and DialogClose is removed. The three Dialog* parts are styled divs that consume no Radix context, so the form boundary can be drawn around them, and EditDialogContainer can leave rendering the footer to the form. The paired rule: any Button inside a form boundary that does not submit must declare type="button".
context: libero-replace.tsx wrapped only DialogBody in its Form, and its footer button was a type="button" outside the form that called form.handleSubmit from onClick. The form's own onSubmit had never fired, and validation could finish only after onClick returned, by which point DialogClose had closed the dialog. At the other end, EditDialogContainer had no DialogFooter at all: the three team forms put their submit buttons at the end of their own Card, inside DialogBody. Only the set-options panel's ActionButton got both things right.

alternatives.option: Wrap only DialogBody and DialogFooter, leaving the header outside
alternatives.reason: The flex cost is identical, since both need exactly one element to add min-h-0 flex-1. Wrapping all three keeps header, body and footer as siblings, which is how DialogContent composed them; wrapping two splits the header onto a different level.

alternatives.option: Accept that libero-replace's validation cannot fire and call onSubmit(form.getValues()) synchronously
alternatives.reason: One line, but the two sites would handle the same thing differently, and the protection would vanish silently the day a field becomes free input.

alternatives.option: Associate the footer button with a form in the body through the form attribute
alternatives.reason: The boundary stays put, but a set of ids has to be maintained. DialogFooter has no reason to sit outside the form; moving the boundary is cheaper than introducing identifiers.

alternatives.option: Put the submit button in DialogFooter only in dialog mode
alternatives.reason: The team forms serve both the @modal and (workspace) routes. Branching would give one form two structures, and DialogBody and DialogFooter are only padded divs on a full page.

consequences: When validation fails, the browser and RHF never call the success path, so not closing is a result of the structure rather than something code has to remember.
libero-replace.tsx's dead form submission path became the path that actually runs.
EditDialogContainer stopped wrapping its children in DialogBody; the forms render DialogBody and DialogFooter themselves in both the dialog and the full-page route.
The inserted form needs min-h-0 flex-1, or DialogContent's flex chain breaks and DialogBody loses its scrollable height.
Button has no default type, so a <Button onClick> inside a form boundary is an implicit submit button; the back button in game/new's DialogTitle is the standing example and declares type="button".

The player edit page is the one exception: the membership section's invite flow has its own <form>, and a basic-information boundary wrapping the footer would nest it, so its save button stays in the section until membership management moves off that page.
revisitTriggers: A submit button appears whose target cannot be expressed by a single form boundary, such as one footer submitting two independent forms.
Button defaults to type="button", so the paired rule no longer relies on people remembering it.
Membership management moves off the player edit page; its save button then moves into DialogFooter.
